mechanism_narrative: Persistent decline in WORKPLACES mobility (-16.3% at t-0w) signals sustained remote work adoption. This reduces commuter foot traffic through retail zones, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks despite any absolute mobility gains.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -10.0% to -16.3% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds mean over last 28 days by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (+11.1% at t-0w, up from +9.3%) indicates households spending more time at home. This behavioral shift crowds out discretionary retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks as home-based consumption substitutes for out-of-home retail.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 10.5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 1 percentage point over the next 28 days when RESIDENTIAL remains above 10.5%.

RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next four weeks unless TRANSIT recovers by at least 5 percentage points.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -10% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -5% over the next 28 days while TRANSIT stays below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between elevated RESIDENTIAL (+11.1%) and depressed TRANSIT (-15.6%) creates a compound confinement effect. Households both stay home longer and lack convenient transit access to retail, producing a multiplicative suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds -7%, indicating the interaction did not suppress retail as predicted.
